reuse.why: Builds on the existing shared getScheduledAmount and the existing getApproxNumberThreshold, and routes the server copies (forecast, updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, schedule-template, API model) through one getExpectedAmount; only the preview path keeps its own dispatch.

duplication.why: Removes five inline midpoint copies in favour of one helper, but computeSchedulePreviewTransactions keeps its own null/number/range ternary around the helper.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules next to getScheduledAmount, the API field is computed in scheduleModel.toExternal, and the list type is declared alongside the API models.

scope.why: Edits are limited to the amount rule, its callers, the API list field and release notes.

maintainability.why: One clear definition of the expected amount, though the preview site and UI callers that omit the op can silently diverge for approximate amounts, and getExpectedAmount/getScheduledAmount are two overlapping entry points.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions: returns schedule._amount directly for numeric amounts instead of letting getExpectedAmount apply the isapprox rule.

disguised_duplication.where: The only leftover is the preview ternary, which is a visible remnant of the old dispatch rather than a disguised copy.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an op parameter and getExpectedAmount an isapprox branch (both reasonable); computeSchedulePreviewTransactions bypasses the helper for numeric amounts, and desktop-client callers other than Balance never pass the op.
